newsitem.title: GERMANY: Traders see upside in IBIS DAX to 3,700 points.
newsitem.headline: Traders see upside in IBIS DAX to 3,700 points.

text.p: German equity traders said on Wednesday that there was upside in the IBIS DAX index to around 3,700 points in the short-term, but that gains would be capped at that level in the current jittery atmosphere.
The IBIS DAX index stood at 3,648.56 points in afternoon electronic trade, while the June DAX future was down seven points at 3,655.50 points.

"My mid-term target is 4,000 points, but I don't think that will happen until there is a decision on petroleum tax. 3,7000 will act as a cap, but then again, predictions keep getting broken these days," a Frankfurt trader said.

In a series of statements over the morning, both Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the German government and the Bundesbank had reached a way of proceeding on a planned revaluation of central bank assets.
He also said that he and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer would do their best to have windfall funds created by the revaluation transferred to Bonn from 1998 and not earlier.
The decision had a fairly neutral effect on shares, despite the fact that uncertainty about the future of European currency union had translated into negative sentiment in the equity market of late.
Among winners over the day was tyre-maker Continental AG, which traded off highs later on, up 55 pfennigs at 39.60 marks, having earlier hit 40.50 marks.

The German financial newsletter Platow Brief said Conti expected to report a distinct increase in 1997 profit at its annual meeting, which lifted the share earlier, while the group said at its annual meeting afterwards that it expected earnings to grow strongly in 1997.
Germany's large utilities were also higher early on, enjoying a cyclical upturn, although they pared gains as the day went on.
Viag AG fell later to trade up 3.30 marks, or 0.42 percent, at 783.30 marks, while Veba was up 88 pfennigs, or 0.90 percent, at 98.10 marks.
Dollar strength also boosted car stocks, particularly VW AG, which rose 23 marks, or 1.93 percent, to 1,190 marks.

Shares in Deutsche Telekom AG were higher after Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said the sale of the government stake in the company would be done in a way that would not upset shares.
Telekom shares rose 38 pfennigs, or nearly one percent, at 38.60 marks.
Privatisation talk also boosted airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG, but this came off highs over the day and by late trade were up 35 pfennigs, or 1.2 percent, at 29.60 marks.
Shares in engineer Thyssen AG rose 1.10 marks, around a quarter percent, at 407 marks after a positive reaction to an analysts meeting, analysts said.
